summary: Documents a Cisco-developed, widely deployed measurement protocol for network performance, including latency, delay variation, and packet loss, using UDP probes. It was published so other vendors could interoperate. It is informational, not an Internet standard.

eli5.summary: Like sending little test balls back and forth across a playground to see how long each takes and whether any get lost, so you know how good the path is.

subtitle: A protocol for measuring network latency, delay variation, and packet loss using UDP test traffic.

tldr.problem: Network operators need to measure service quality—latency, jitter, and packet loss—to verify service-level agreements and diagnose network health. Existing passive measurement is limited; active measurement with standard protocols is needed.
tldr.mechanism: The Cisco SLA Protocol uses two phases: a Control phase where a sender requests to open a UDP port on a responder, and a Measurement phase where test packets are exchanged with precise timestamps. Results allow calculation of round-trip time, one-way latency, jitter, and loss.
tldr.outcome: Vendors can interoperate using this protocol. Operators can measure service levels and validate SLAs, and applications can simulate UDP traffic like voice and video over RTP.

today: RFC 6812 is an Informational RFC documenting the Cisco SLA Protocol for vendor interoperability. It has not been obsoleted. The protocol is widely deployed in Cisco equipment and is used by network operators to verify service levels.

sections.title: Active Performance Measurement
sections.content:
Network performance measurement is essential for monitoring service levels and verifying SLAs. Active measurement generates synthetic test packets to derive metrics like latency, jitter (delay variation), and packet loss. This contrasts with passive measurement, which analyzes real traffic.

The Cisco SLA Protocol is a performance measurement protocol that has been widely deployed by Cisco and is being published for vendor interoperability. It can test L2 and L3 networks and simulate applications running atop layer 3. The UDP-Measurement variant described here is compatible with UDP traffic and can simulate voice or video encoded in RTP frames within UDP.
sections.eli5: Instead of watching real users, network managers send test packets back and forth to check how good the network is. It's like a coach throwing practice balls to measure a player's speed.

sections.title: Control Phase: Setting Up Measurement
sections.content:
The protocol has two distinct phases. In the Control Phase, a Sender initiates a Control-Request message to UDP port 1167 on a Responder, requesting that a UDP measurement port be opened for a specified duration. The request includes an Authentication CSLD (Command, Status, Length, Data section) and a UDP-Measurement CSLD containing source and destination addresses and ports for the upcoming measurement phase.

The Responder validates the request (verifies the sender's identity) and replies with a Control-Response indicating success or a status error such as 'Port in use' or 'Authentication Failure'. Only upon success does the Measurement Phase begin.
sections.eli5: First, one machine asks permission: 'Can I send test packets to port X for the next 10 seconds?' The other machine checks the password and says yes or no.

sections.title: Measurement Phase: Exchanging Test Traffic
sections.content:
Upon receiving a successful Control-Response, the Measurement Phase begins. The Sender transmits a stream of Measurement-Request packets at regular intervals (configurable number of milliseconds apart). Each request carries precise timestamps (following RFC 5905 Network Time Protocol format or IEEE 1588 Precision Time Protocol format).

Each Measurement-Request contains: Sender Send Time, Responder Receive Time (filled by responder), Responder Send Time (filled by responder), Sender Receive Time (filled by sender), and Clock Offset fields from both sides to account for time synchronization differences. The responder echoes back a Measurement-Response with these fields updated.

From these four timestamps, the Sender can calculate round-trip delay, one-way latency (with clock offset adjustment), and by analyzing sequences, derive jitter and packet loss statistics.
sections.eli5: Test packets ping-pong back and forth, each one stamped with the exact time it was sent and received. By comparing timestamps, both sides can calculate how fast and how reliable the path is.

sections.title: Authentication and Security
sections.content:
The Authentication CSLD in the Control Phase supports three modes: No Authentication, SHA256, or HMAC-SHA-256. When security is enabled, a random number field helps prevent dictionary attacks, and a message authentication digest protects the control message integrity.

The RFC recommends IPsec protection for both Control and Measurement traffic. For Senders, the policy 'Initiate IPsec, from me to any, destination port UDP 1167' protects control messages. For Responders, the policy 'Require IPsec, from any to me, destination port UDP 1167' enforces protection. Measurement traffic can be protected similarly once the Control Phase succeeds.
sections.eli5: The password can be simple or cryptographically strong. Both sides can also wrap the test packets in encryption to prevent snooping.

sections.title: Future Extensions and Registries
sections.content:
The protocol is designed for extensibility. Future Measurement-Type CSLDs can be added to support new types of tests beyond UDP-Measurement. The RFC defines several IANA registries: Version Numbers, CSLD Command Types, Authenticator Modes, Roles, Measurement Types, Status Types, and Address Family Types. Unassigned ranges are available for new tests, and Private Use and Experimental Use ranges exist for vendor extensions.

A Control Phase followed by a Measurement Phase can be repeated to enable continuous measurement throughout a device's lifetime.
sections.eli5: The protocol can be expanded later to measure other types of traffic or add new features. Think of it like a game that starts simple but can add new rules later.
